newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian debt futures pare hefty SYCOM gains.
newsitem.headline: Australian debt futures pare hefty SYCOM gains.

text.p: Australian bond futures slipped from the perky levels seen in the pre-weekend SYCOM session as the benchmark 10-year bond yields failed to sustain a break below 7.0 percent.
Traders said the market had over-extended itself in thin after hours trade, although speculation of a further easing in monetary policy would limit the size of any pullback.
"I suspect we are going to see this scenairo until the Reserve Bank finally does cut rates. People will be jumping on any pullback at the short end," one trader said.

Talk of a cut in official 5.5 percent rates has been prominent since the extremely weak May labour force report just under two weeks ago, which followed several other poor indicators and suggested growth expectations might not be met.

Bill futures have practically priced in a 50 basis point easing, although such a move is seen as most likely to occur after the July 1 RBA board and the Federal Open Market Committee meetings on July 1 and 2.
The September 10-year bond futures contract had ended SYCOM at 93.000, which had taken the October 2007 bond yield just a shade below 7.0 percent.
However, a sustained move below 7.0 percent is likely to be dependent on the rate cut, traders said.

A firm U.S. Treasury market on Friday, which was largely driven by technical factors and took the 30-year bond yield to 6.64 percent at one stage, supported the local futures rally in after hours trade.
While local rate cut hopes will continue to give an underlying bid tone, the market will again suffer from a dearth of data which will again limit turnover, traders added.

Spreads to the dollar bloc showed a mild narrowing bias despite the local market's initial pull-back. New Zealand debt remained under pressure ahead of this Thursday's budget and the RBNZ's monetary policy statement on Friday.
